title: Do you wake up at the same time every night? It's nothing to worry about, but if you want to fall back asleep, don't check the time
subhead: 'Strange Nights' (6/7). Everyone wakes up several times a night, most often at the end of a sleep cycle. Deep sleepers don't remember it, while others struggle to go back to sleep. To understand this, let's look at how sleep cycles work.

title: 'Fjord' by Cristian Mungiu, Cannes Palme d'Or winner: A clash of opposing worlds
subhead: A deeply religious Romanian evangelical family, newly settled in a small Norwegian town, clashes with the country's liberal principles and ultimately the courts when the couple is suspected of child abuse.

title: Fires and 'megaboats' fuel tensions over Channel crossings in northern France

subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (3/6). Radio Begum, 'a radio station made by women for women,' is the only connection to the outside world for many Afghan women. It is one of several projects to help young girls access education under the Taliban regime.

title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: Tiananmen Square massacre: Le Monde reveals unseen footage of the Chinese regime's violent repression
subhead: Art historian Nathalie Trouveroy shared footage with Le Monde from her personal archives of the Tiananmen Square protests, shedding new light on how the Chinese regime violently repressed the student protests in June 1989.
